quotes.text: Customize the reboot time window for your readers.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: Instead, the readers reboot randomly within the configured time period.
Stripe sets the new reboot window within 10 minutes.
The value must be different than the `start_hour`.

findings: The November 7, 2026 base capture is a reader reboot-window introduction and an index of Dashboard and API variants. It establishes neither the procedural bodies nor a new device behavior.

The May 1, 2026 full guide describes a merchant setting a smart-reader window via local or inherited Dashboard configuration or Configuration API create/update. By default smart readers reboot every 24 hours at midnight. They use the registered location's local time and stagger reboots randomly during the specified window.

The May guide permits different start/end integers 0–23. A lower start is same-day and a larger start crosses midnight. Stripe sets the window within 10 minutes, and a reader already rebooted for the day uses the next period. The old summary captures most of this but omits the unequal-endpoint guard.
substantive_changes: No functional delta is established. November substitutes linked Markdown variants for May's embedded Dashboard and API bodies. The feature description remains.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Preserve the May default and registered location timezone, random staggering, two location-centric Dashboard paths with Update then Apply changes, API create/update on Configuration, unequal integer hour endpoints with same-day or crossing-midnight interpretation, and within-ten-minutes versus next-period condition.
conflicts: Current summary presents May timing without a date, shortens 'within 10 minutes' to '10 minutes', and omits the inequality for the two integer hours. Keep these as May guide facts. The passcode wording in the old location-selection step is inconsistent with the surrounding Reboot time steps and is not a separate prerequisite.

The separately captured November Configuration create and update references describe an optional reboot_window for readers with customized reboot support (create lines 50–51 and update lines 64–65). That separate scope does not supply the November reboot variant's timing or nested hour constraints.
unresolved_questions: The November index does not resolve whether device coverage, registered timezone, default, nested constraints, timing or variant-specific UI steps changed. A feature or constraint removal cannot be inferred from omission of those bodies.

findings: Link November as Dashboard/API navigation and retain May as operational evidence. Keep the reciprocal stripe-terminal-hardware-orders route and link the Terminal Configurations source for context.
conflicts: Preserve the May unequal-hour rule and qualify setting time as within ten minutes, with the already-rebooted condition. Keep November API corroboration limited to field and compatible reader scope.
source_assessments.reason: November adds a useful routing index. The May guide remains the pinned operational source and supports a missing input validation condition in the summary.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/fleet/reboot-time, source-stripe-terminal-reboot-time should describe the November 7, 2026 capture as a reboot-window introduction with separate Dashboard and API routes. See new raw lines 5-14. These bytes establish neither default schedule nor configuration or reboot transitions. The May 1, 2026 full guide says smart readers default to a midnight reboot every 24 hours, interpret the window in the registered location's local time and randomly stagger reboots within the configured period. In Dashboard the merchant edits or overrides the relevant configuration for a location, selects start/end, updates and applies the changes. Stripe sets the new window within 10 minutes. A reader that already rebooted that day uses the next period. See old raw lines 8-12 and old raw lines 18-39. API callers can create or update Configuration with reboot_window. Each hour is an integer 0–23 and end_hour must differ from start_hour. A lower start is same-day and a greater start crosses midnight. See old raw lines 45-83. The summary mostly tracks May, but should state the unequal-hour guard and preserve within ten minutes rather than suggesting a fixed delay.
